silhouette.reason: The furry body and hump read as a bear, but the head is a flat wedge with a long, thin pointed snout and tiny ears: from 3/4 it reads as a wombat or wolverine, not a dished bear face.
fixes: enlarge the head ~15%, shorten and widen the muzzle and raise the forehead so the dished bear profile reads

proportions.reason: The trunk is long and the legs short for a brown bear in SIDE; the neck is short but the head is undersized against the hump.
fixes: shorten the trunk ~10% and lengthen the legs ~8% (plantigrade stance, hind feet under the hips)

materials.reason: Fur cards cover the body now, but the face is smooth tan plastic with a hard seam to the fur, and the paws are pale tan socks with no dark pads or claws.
fixes: extend fur cards onto the face edge and cheeks; darker brown muzzle
dark leathery paw pads and dark claws; glossy nose and eyes

detail.reason: Fur cards break the back and belly outline; the face has no brow/cheek planes, there are no visible claws, and the ears are tiny nubs.
fixes: claws on each paw as curved cones
sharper brow and cheek planes, rounder ears

wear.reason: A pink scar on the face and a rubbed pale patch on the shoulder; paws are clean and pale, no mud.
fixes: mud on the paws and lower legs (grime with the ground mask)
matted wet fur on the belly fringe

lod.reason: FAR LOD2 keeps the outline but the legs become straight tubes and the coat breaks into angular light/dark patches.
fixes: LOD2 legs from the sculpt with an inflate instead of tubes; average the coat colour per face

technical.reason: QA clean; 123k / 25k / 2k triangles over 4 draws: LOD0 is heavy for what shows, much of it fur cards on the back.
fixes: cap LOD0 near 100k by coarsening the fur-card density on the back
